routing_warnings.description: The same message also introduces hook variations and reuse of a body clip, which should be represented under the narrower hook-variation Requirement rather than as a quota-value change.
The newly permitted B-roll and its required use are independently governed by the B-roll integration Requirement; the message otherwise restates the existing Teyron YouTube source.
Reusing a body clip with different openings and deriving many ideas from one long video concerns hook variations rather than changing the permitted source material.
The request to find better and more impactful moments concerns moment impact rather than whether a lesson or story is complete.
The unresolved Instagram account tag concerns post metadata rather than whether approved clips must be published.
The Reel URL also supports the independent requirement to report the published link.
The requirement for at least ten approved posted videos establishes a payment threshold rather than changing the basic publishing behavior.
The rejected-quality observation and new three-clip test belong to the qualification Requirement; only the changed and deferred Lead Clipper pathway is represented here.
The communication failure described as a reason for termination belongs to the progress-communication Requirement; the contract termination itself removes the Lead Clipper role.
The permission to reuse a body clip two to three times by changing its hook belongs to the separate hook-variations Requirement.
The separate clause permitting shorter clip styles concerns clip-duration rules rather than hook variations and body-clip reuse.
The hook-training clause concerns finding strong hooks and should not be folded into the body-clip reuse Requirement.
The criticism that clips used fragments rather than complete lessons or stories concerns standalone teaching completeness, not the independent impactfulness of the selected moments.
The instruction that clips deliver a full lesson rather than being cut in half concerns teaching-moment completeness.
The instruction to report back after posting concerns client-facing publication reporting rather than updating the Notion tracking card.
The request to send the published link belongs to the separate Reel-link reporting Requirement.
The freelancer sends the published Reel link to the client, but this does not establish that the Notion card was updated.
The instruction to record the Reel link and posting date in Notion belongs to Notion posting tracking rather than direct link reporting to the client.
The upload-completion claim concerns publication of the approved clip, not the independently completed act of sending its link.
The Instagram Reel URL is evidence of reporting a published link, not evidence that the required caption, hashtags, and account tag were used.

missing_requirement_candidates.suggested_title: Initial Approved-Post Threshold for Payment Release
missing_requirement_candidates.description: The client establishes a temporary requirement of at least 10 approved and posted videos before full payment; this is distinct from the recurring 100-approved-clips monthly quota.
Creating and branding the dedicated Instagram account is independently required before publishing and is not represented in the frozen inventory.
Posting one clip per day between 6 PM and 9 PM is an independently changeable scheduling behavior not represented in the frozen inventory.
